item.title: China-aligned hackers used AI tool to target over 2,250 cloud environments worldwide

item.content:encoded:
China-aligned hackers used AI tool to target over 2,250 cloud environments worldwide Citing findings published by Microsoft on October 21, the report said the hacking group Storm-0940, which Microsoft has tracked since 2021, compromised credentials associated with ConnectWise’s Cloud Backup application. ANI | Updated: 26-10-2026 18:41 IST | Created: 26-10-2026 18:41 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

A China-aligned hacking group used an artificial intelligence (AI) tool to accelerate cyberattacks against hundreds of organisations worldwide, including an incident involving US technology company ConnectWise, according to a report by The Epoch Times (TET). Citing findings published by Microsoft on October 21, the report said the hacking group Storm-0940, which Microsoft has tracked since 2021, compromised credentials associated with ConnectWise’s Cloud Backup application. The stolen credentials potentially enabled attackers to exploit access already authorised by customers using Microsoft’s cloud services. The group reportedly used ARTEX, a Chinese-developed AI security-testing tool, to automate scanning, password attempts and exploitation of application permissions. Its targets included government agencies, defence contractors, financial institutions, technology companies and other organisations. According to the TET report, Storm-0940 attempted to access more than 2,250 customer cloud environments through compromised ConnectWise applications. Microsoft clarified that this figure represented attempted access, not confirmed breaches. In several cases, the attackers obtained privileged access to cloud systems in less than three hours after initial targeting. Microsoft observed the group examining cloud resources, modifying application credentials and attempting to change permissions. Such changes could allow unauthorised access to persist even after the original compromised credentials were disabled. However, Microsoft noted that successful access did not necessarily mean customer data had been stolen. ConnectWise confirmed unauthorised access to credentials associated with its Cloud Backup service, formerly known as SkyKick. In an October 25 update, the company said existing backup archives remained encrypted, isolated and preserved, with no indication they had been compromised. It also reported no evidence that other ConnectWise products or services were affected. The incident disrupted access to Cloud Backup while investigations and restoration work continued. ConnectWise planned to begin allowing partners to restore data from existing backups on October 26, followed by phased re-enrolment. Customers were advised to keep affected application connections disabled until restoration instructions arrived and to check their Microsoft 365 environments for suspicious activity. As cited by TET, ARTEX was originally developed to help security professionals identify weaknesses in computer systems. The tool uses AI to plan operations, direct other tools and pursue different ways into networks with limited human intervention. Microsoft said the automation enabled Storm-0940 to conduct operations simultaneously and exploit stolen credentials rapidly. Its researchers warned that the speed of the activity left defenders with very little time to respond to alerts. The report noted that ARTEX had previously been identified in attacks involving South Korean financial institutions and Japanese companies. Japanese investigators reportedly found the tool on six overseas servers targeting approximately 80 businesses. Microsoft did not attribute those earlier attacks to Storm-0940. According to TET, ARTEX creator Autumn-27 condemned the tool’s misuse in an October 8 statement, denied involvement in the reported attacks and announced that public updates and maintenance would end. Chinese cybersecurity company ThreatBook said on October 16 that ARTEX began as a personal project by its RedAgents product lead. The company acknowledged misuse of the open-source version in major financial-sector security incidents and said it lacked built-in security controls. TET reported that it contacted ThreatBook, Microsoft and ConnectWise for further comment, but none had responded by publication time. (ANI)

item.title: "Makes no difference to us": Iran’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson Baghaei compares Israeli election to movie 'Dr. Strangelove'
item.description: Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei has said that the outcome of the upcoming Israeli election will make "no difference" to Iran, comparing the contest between political factions in ...
item.content:encoded:
"Makes no difference to us": Iran’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson Baghaei compares Israeli election to movie 'Dr. Strangelove' Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei has said that the outcome of the upcoming Israeli election will make "no difference" to Iran, comparing the contest between political factions in Israel to the 1964 satirical film "Dr. Strangelove," which revolves around the threat of a nuclear catastrophe. ANI | Updated: 26-10-2026 14:38 IST | Created: 26-10-2026 14:38 IST

Iranian Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Esmail Baghaei (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

Country:

Iran

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei has said that the outcome of the upcoming Israeli election will make "no difference" to Iran, comparing the contest between political factions in Israel to the 1964 satirical film "Dr. Strangelove," which revolves around the threat of a nuclear catastrophe. According to Iran's ISNA news agency, Baghaei made the remarks during his weekly press conference on Monday while responding to a question about statements by Israeli authorities regarding the possibility of Iran taking preemptive action to disrupt the Israeli election process. "I don't think there will be an election there. There, like in the movie Strangelove, there is competition between different gangs to commit more evil; in other words, it is a competition between different people to commit more murders," Baghaei said. He added that the identity of the person who ultimately takes charge of Israel would make no difference to Tehran. "It makes no difference to us, in such an environment and election, who ultimately becomes the helmsman of a regime whose history has brought nothing but killing and violence to our region. The genocide of Palestinians has continued for these 80 years. The fact that the Zionist regime threatens others and uses rhetoric out of desperation is part of the evil of this regime," he said. Baghaei also accused Israel of being skilled in false flag operations and said Iran was closely monitoring developments, while warning that its armed forces were prepared to defend the country. "What I can assure you is that, regardless of rhetoric, we are carefully monitoring developments and our powerful armed forces will not hesitate to defend Iran's territory," he said. He further asserted that Iran was in a state of war and would exercise its right to defend its sovereignty and independence. "In these circumstances, we are in a state of war, so in such a situation, Iran will certainly not hesitate to exercise its inherent right to legitimately defend the Iranian identity, the country's territorial integrity, and Iran's independence," Baghaei said. The reference to 'Dr. Strangelove,' Stanley Kubrick's 1964 black comedy formally titled 'Dr. Strangelove or: How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the Bomb,' invokes a story centred on the danger of nuclear war. The film follows an unauthorised nuclear attack ordered by a US Air Force general and the desperate efforts of American leaders to prevent a global catastrophe after learning that the Soviet Union possesses a "doomsday" weapon. His remarks come as Israeli President Isaac Herzog has affirmed that any decision on who will lead Israel after Tuesday's election will be taken without any external pressure. Herzog who will be called upon to invite one of the Knesset Members to form a government made the remarks amidst a second endorsement from US President Donald Trump for incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his Likud-led coalition. Speaking to US network MS NOW, Herzog said he would not bow to pressure from President Donald Trump. “I don’t think the President of the United States or anybody else can intervene in my discretion; the discretion has to be based on certain facts, and we will see what the facts are...There will be a lot of pressure, though, regardless,” he said. Herzog said he has “huge respect” for Trump and welcomes any dialogue, but the decision will be his, and his alone. Meanwhile, ahead of the elections, Israel's Channel 12 reported on Sunday night that there appears to be a confrontation brewing between Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu and the IDF Chief of Staff General Eyal Zamir over launching attacks on Iran. In response, Israel's Defence Minister Israel Katz on Monday denied reports of a confrontation between Netanyahu and Zamir over possible military action against Iran, saying Israel had no intention of launching an "attack" before the country's elections, according to The Times of Israel. "The reports of disagreements between the political leadership and the IDF on Iran are completely baseless and false," Katz said in a statement. “I state unequivocally that Israel had no intention of initiating an attack on Iran before the elections in Israel, while making clear that if Iran attacks Israel, we will respond with great force,” he said, adding that "all reports on this matter are completely false." (ANI)

item.title: Pakistan’s food supply falls short of healthy diet needs, FAO warns; vegetables and fruits face major gaps
item.description: Pakistan’s food supply remains significantly misaligned with national dietary guidelines, with persistent shortages of vegetables, fruits, roots and tubers, and pulses, while cereals and sugar exceed ...
item.content:encoded:
Pakistan’s food supply falls short of healthy diet needs, FAO warns; vegetables and fruits face major gaps Pakistan’s food supply remains significantly misaligned with national dietary guidelines, with persistent shortages of vegetables, fruits, roots and tubers, and pulses, while cereals and sugar exceed dietary requirements, according to a Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) policy brief cited by Dawn. ANI | Updated: 26-10-2026 14:38 IST | Created: 26-10-2026 14:38 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Pakistan’s food supply remains significantly misaligned with national dietary guidelines, with persistent shortages of vegetables, fruits, roots and tubers, and pulses, while cereals and sugar exceed dietary requirements, according to a Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) policy brief cited by Dawn. The policy brief, titled “Food Supply for Healthy Diets in Pakistan,” highlights the need to ensure equitable access to diverse, nutritious, safe and affordable food, particularly as more than 60 per cent of Pakistanis cannot afford a healthy diet, Dawn reported. The report warned that the imbalance contributes to high levels of malnutrition, while diet-related noncommunicable diseases continue to rise alongside persistent undernutrition. Pakistan adopted its food-based dietary guidelines in 2018, establishing evidence-based recommendations on the types and quantities of food required for healthy diets. However, the FAO brief stressed that efforts to encourage healthier eating would remain insufficient unless nutritious foods were also available and accessible to the population. According to Dawn, the assessment compared Pakistan’s annual food supply with population-level requirements across 10 food groups identified in the national dietary guidelines, examining trends between 2010 and 2023 to determine the extent of supply gaps and surpluses. The FAO assessment identified persistent shortages in several essential food groups, particularly vegetables, roots and tubers, fruits, and legumes and pulses. According to the figures cited by Dawn, Pakistan’s estimated vegetable supply gap widened from a range of 10.9 million to 17.8 million tonnes in 2010 to between 13 million and 21.6 million tonnes in 2023. The shortfall in fruits also increased substantially during the period, rising from an estimated 1.9 million to 10.3 million tonnes in 2010 to between 3.9 million and 14.3 million tonnes in 2023. In contrast, the supply of milk and milk products, meat and eggs showed improvement. Fats and oils also moved from a small supply gap in 2010 into the estimated required range in subsequent years, the report said. The findings highlight a disparity between the availability of essential nutritious foods and the country’s dietary requirements, even as cereals and sugar remain in excess of recommended levels. Pakistan’s growing population is expected to place further pressure on its food and agricultural systems. According to the FAO brief cited by Dawn, the country’s population increased from 189.3 million in 2010 to 235.2 million in 2023 and is projected to reach approximately 330 million by 2050. The report warned that population growth, alongside climate change and other challenges, is likely to intensify demands on the agrifood system, making improvements in food production, distribution and accessibility increasingly important. To address the imbalance, the FAO has recommended coordinated fiscal and regulatory measures to align agricultural production and trade priorities with national nutritional needs. The recommendations include improving food distribution systems, reducing post-harvest losses and food waste, and strengthening demand for healthier food products. The brief also called for updating Pakistan’s food-based dietary guidelines to incorporate nutrition, public health and environmental priorities. It recommended expanding nutrition education and behaviour-change initiatives to encourage healthier dietary choices. Among the proposed measures are evidence-based taxes on beverages and foods high in sugar, salt and unhealthy fats, alongside front-of-package nutrition labelling to help consumers make informed decisions about their food purchases. The FAO further urged greater agricultural investment in vegetables, fruits, pulses, roots and tubers, while recommending support for milk production in certain regions. Additional measures include providing incentives to food processors to meet quality standards and reformulate products to reduce their salt, sugar and unhealthy fat content, Dawn reported. (ANI)

item.title: Chinese automakers expand manufacturing in Europe to avoid EU tariffs amid rising domestic competition: Report
item.description: Chinese automakers are expanding their manufacturing presence in Europe amid intensifying competition and excess production capacity in their domestic market, as per a report by The Korea Herald.
item.content:encoded:
Chinese automakers expand manufacturing in Europe to avoid EU tariffs amid rising domestic competition: Report Chinese automakers are expanding their manufacturing presence in Europe amid intensifying competition and excess production capacity in their domestic market, as per a report by The Korea Herald. ANI | Updated: 26-10-2026 13:42 IST | Created: 26-10-2026 13:42 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

Country:

South Korea

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Chinese automakers are expanding their manufacturing presence in Europe amid intensifying competition and excess production capacity in their domestic market, as per a report by The Korea Herald. According to the report, Chinese automakers, including BYD, Chery and Geely, are shifting production closer to European markets amid intense domestic competition and excess manufacturing capacity. Beyond avoiding European Union (EU) tariffs, these companies are leveraging underutilised factories and local partnerships to establish a long-term presence in Europe's automotive industry. “The expansion marks a new phase in China's global automotive ambitions, testing whether its advantages in cost, scale and electric vehicle technology can be replicated overseas,” the report said. At the same time, it noted, for Hyundai Motor Group, which has spent decades building a European manufacturing network, the transformation brings a “formidable new challenge” as Chinese rivals increasingly compete on its turf. On the other hand, BYD is leading China's localization push, preparing to begin production at its new plant in Szeged, Hungary, this year. The facility, designed for an eventual annual capacity of 300,000 vehicles, will become BYD's first European passenger-car production base. It is expected to manufacture compact electric models, including the Dolphin Surf and Atto 2. Hence, local production offers a significant advantage in navigating EU trade restrictions, it noted. Chinese-made battery electric vehicles (EVs) are subject to a standard 10 per cent import duty in the European Union (EU), along with additional countervailing tariffs ranging from 7.8 per cent to 35.3 per cent, depending on the manufacturer. BYD faces an additional tariff of 17 per cent, while Geely and SAIC Motor face levies of 18.8 per cent and 35.3 per cent, respectively. Thus, setting up manufacturing facilities within the EU would enable Chinese automakers to avoid these additional import tariffs, lower shipping costs and strengthen ties with local suppliers. Notably, other Chinese manufacturers are pursuing similar strategies. SAIC Motor, which sells vehicles primarily under its MG brand, has explored plans for a European production facility as it seeks to reduce reliance on imports from China, the report said. Additionally, “Chinese automakers are increasingly forming alliances with established manufacturers that are struggling with sluggish demand, costly electrification investments and underused production capacity.” It should also be noted that Chinese brands' European sales jumped 90.6 percent year-on-year to 531,862 vehicles in the first half of 2026, The Korea Herald reported, citing market research firm MarkLines. “Chinese manufacturers are expanding beyond battery-electric vehicles into plug-in hybrids and conventional hybrids,” it noted. While this shift may help the struggling European factories stay open, it also raises questions about the region's growing reliance on China. (ANI)
